# QA Story 834: Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board

Run a full QA session for this story. Two phases: write a testing brief,
then execute it. The playbook below has the detailed procedure.

**App URL:** Run `mix run -e 'IO.puts(CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url())'`.

## Story description

As a cleaning business owner, I want a single-screen weekly board showing every cleaner's schedule where I can assign/reassign jobs, so that I can dispatch and rebalance the week at a glance instead of clicking through tabs. (Research: MaidCentral users explicitly wish for "every employee's schedule for the entire week on a single screen" — pain-points §1.1, §4)

## Acceptance criteria

- See the whole week at a glance
- Reassign a job to another cleaner
- Block reassigning onto a conflicting slot
- Dispatch an unassigned job from the board
- Reassignment reaches the cleaner's schedule

1	# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	## App Overview
4	
5	Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).
6	
7	## Tools Registry
8	
9	### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)
10	
11	Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.
12	
13	### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)
14	
15	Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.
16	
17	### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)
18	
19	Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.
20	
21	## Seed Strategy
22	
23	Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:
24	
25	- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.

# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

# QA Story Workflow

The `qa_story` agent task is a per-story QA cycle: write a brief, then execute
it against the running app. The project-wide QA plan
(`.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md`) is a prerequisite — produced upstream by
`qa_setup`, not written here.

QA completion is recorded by a DB-backed attempt via `submit_qa_result`. There
is no result.md file in the loop. Findings are filed via `create_issue` as
they're uncovered and linked into the attempt by id.

## Phase 1: Testing brief

**Artifact:** `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md`

The brief is the concrete plan for testing this story — which tools to use,
how to authenticate, what scenarios to test, and what to assert.

Procedure:

1. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for App Overview, Tools Registry,
   auth strategy, and Seed Strategy.
2. Run seed scripts to verify setup works for this story.
3. If this story needs additional seeds or plan updates, make them now
   and update plan.md (don't fork into a story-specific plan).
4. Read the BDD spec files listed in the prompt. They have selectors,
   test data, and assertions.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source and
   spec to understand the feature.
6. Write the brief to `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` matching
   the `qa_story_brief` document spec from the prompt.

## Phase 2: Execute tests

There is no `result.md` artifact in this phase. Findings flow through
`create_issue` as you discover them; the run ends with one call to
`submit_qa_result`.

### Tool rules — pick by Phoenix pipeline, not by guess

- **UI / LiveView (`:browser` pipeline):** MCP browser tools only.
  Navigate, click, type, screenshot. Log in via the browser (credentials
  and login steps are in the plan).
- **API endpoints (`:api` pipeline):** `curl` with API key headers.
  ALWAYS single-line commands. Use
  `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` for API-key auth.
- **NEVER** use curl with session cookies or CSRF tokens for
  browser-authenticated routes. If a route is behind
  `:require_authenticated_user`, test it with MCP browser tools.

### Testing approach

- Capture a screenshot at each key state (initial load, after
  interactions, success/error states). Save to
  `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/screenshots/`. Screenshots are evidence
  and remain valuable — attach the path in the issue description for
  any finding that ships a screenshot.
- After scripted scenarios, explore freely: unexpected inputs, edge
  cases, empty states, anything that feels off.
- Reference existing scripts in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/` by path
  rather than inlining shell commands.

### Filing findings

The moment you observe something wrong — a broken UI, a 500, a missing
feature, an unexpected behavior — call `create_issue` and hold the
returned id. Don't accumulate findings in a notepad. Don't write them
into a markdown file. The DB issue is the canonical record.

- `title` — short, scannable.
- `severity` — critical / high / medium / low / info.
- `scope` — `app` for app-under-development bugs; `qa` for QA infrastructure
  problems; `docs` for docs gaps; (`framework` is a server-side concept and
  not selectable from the local list_issues filter, but `create_issue`
  itself supports it for harness issues).
- `story_id` — the story this finding relates to, when relevant.
- `description` — the reproduction, the expected vs actual, file paths,
  and any screenshot or evidence path.

If a finding is a duplicate of an existing issue (you'll see them in the
prompt's "Existing Issues" section), don't refile.

### Procedure

1. Read the brief at `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` for the
   complete plan.
2. Read `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` for auth strategy and seed commands.
3. Read `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling.md` and `priv/knowledge/qa-tooling/`
   for tool usage patterns.
4. Run seed scripts to set up test data.
5. If a linked component is listed in the prompt, read its source to
   understand implementation details.
6. Execute each test scenario from the brief.
7. Capture screenshots at key states (save to the screenshots directory).
8. For every finding, call `create_issue` immediately and remember the id.
9. If you find a gap in the plan or the brief, fix it in-flight — update
   `plan.md` or `brief.md` rather than working around the gap.
10. Call `submit_qa_result` once at the end with `status`, the structured
    `scenarios` list, and the full `issue_ids` list. Then stop the session.

## What the evaluator does when you stop

The evaluator runs a thin check chain:

1. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/plan.md` exists with required sections.
   (If missing, returns invalid pointing at `qa_setup`.)
2. Validates that `.code_my_spec/qa/<story_id>/brief.md` exists and parses.
3. Checks whether a DB-backed pass attempt exists via
   `CodeMySpec.Qa.qa_complete?/2`. If yes, the requirement is satisfied
   and the session ends.
4. If no DB attempt exists but the brief is valid, feedback is returned
   demanding a `submit_qa_result` call. The requirement does NOT satisfy
   off a brief alone.

## The submit_qa_result contract

```
submit_qa_result(
  task_id: <task_id from start_task>,
  status: "pass" | "partial" | "fail",
  scenarios: [
    %{name: "...", status: "pass|partial|fail", observation: "..."},
    ...
  ],
  issue_ids: [<every id returned from create_issue this run>]
)
```

Rules:

- `status: "pass"` with `issue_ids: []` is allowed — clean pass, nothing to
  file.
- `status: "partial"` or `"fail"` with `issue_ids: []` is **rejected** by
  the tool. File the findings first.
- Only `status: "pass"` satisfies the `qa_complete` requirement. Other
  statuses record an audit row but leave the requirement open.
- Resubmitting on the same `task_id` is allowed — each call creates a new
  attempt; the latest is canonical.

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
    IO.puts("  Created: qa@example.com")
    user
  user ->
    IO.puts("  Exists: qa@example.com")
    user
end

scope = MyApp.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---
IO.puts("\n--- Account ---")
account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

### Patterns

- **Idempotency**: check for existing records before inserting. Use context `get_by` functions or Ecto queries.
- **Use context functions**: call `Accounts.create_user(scope, attrs)` not `Repo.insert(%User{...})`. This ensures validations, associations, and side effects run.
- **Build Scope**: after creating the user, build a `Scope` to pass to all subsequent context calls.
- **Print credentials**: always print login info, URLs, and entity IDs at the end.
- **Multiple scripts**: split into separate files for different scenarios (base entities vs. specific test flows). Each is independently runnable.

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

# Public routes
smoke "/"
smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

# Authenticated routes should redirect to login
smoke "/accounts" 302

exit $FAIL
```

### Tips

- Accept 302 as valid for auth-protected routes when not logged in
- Check for 500s specifically — a 404 or 302 might be expected
- Use `mix phx.routes` output to build the route list
- For authenticated route testing, use Vibium MCP with `browser_restore_storage`

## Phoenix LiveView Login Patterns

Phoenix apps generated with `phx.gen.auth` have specific login patterns that require careful handling. These patterns apply to all Vibium MCP-based QA automation.

### Login page structure

The `/users/log-in` page renders **two separate forms** side by side:
- `#login_form_magic` — email-only form that sends a magic link
- `#login_form_password` — email + password form that submits via `POST /users/log-in`

The password form is often **below the viewport fold** because it comes after the magic link form. You must scroll it into view before interacting, or interaction tools will timeout waiting for the element to be actionable.

### Re-authentication mode

When a user has an existing session (e.g., session expired but cookie remains), Phoenix renders the login page in re-auth mode where the email field has a `readonly` attribute. Detect this and skip the email field:

```
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
```

If the result is `true`, skip the email fill step.

### Reference login sequence (MCP tools)

```
# 1. Navigate to login page
browser_navigate(url: "http://localhost:4000/users/log-in")

# 2. CRITICAL: scroll password form into view — it's below the magic link form
browser_scroll_into_view(selector: "#login_form_password")

# 3. Check for re-auth mode (readonly email field)
browser_evaluate(expression: "document.querySelector('#login_form_password_email')?.hasAttribute('readonly') ?? false")
# If false, fill email:
browser_fill(selector: "#login_form_password_email", text: "qa@example.com")

# 4. Fill password
browser_fill(selector: "#user_password", text: "hello world!")

# 5. Click "Log in and stay logged in"
browser_click(selector: "#login_form_password button[name='user[remember_me]']")

# 6. Wait for page to load after redirect
browser_wait(selector: "body", timeout: 5000)
```

### Reference logout sequence (MCP tools)

# QA Tooling Patterns

Guide for writing QA test infrastructure for Phoenix LiveView apps. Covers Vibium MCP browser automation, seed data scripts, and smoke tests.

## Tool selection: Vibium MCP vs curl

**Use the right tool for the right layer.** Getting this wrong wastes time and creates fragile scripts.

| What you're testing | Tool | Auth mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| UI pages, LiveViews, forms, navigation | **Vibium MCP** | Browser session (login via MCP tools, persist with `browser_storage_state`) | `browser_navigate` + `browser_map` |
| API endpoints (`/api/*`) | **curl** | `X-Api-Key` header, bearer token, or no auth | `curl -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" /api/transactions/1` |
| Webhooks | **curl** | Webhook signature or no auth | `curl -X POST -d '...' /api/webhooks/card-swipe` |
| Smoke tests (route reachability) | **curl** | None (just check HTTP status codes) | `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' /` |

### The golden rule

**Never use curl for session-authenticated routes.** Phoenix session auth requires signed cookies, CSRF tokens, and form POSTs — scraping HTML for tokens is fragile and wrong. If the route is behind `:browser` pipeline + `:require_authenticated_user`, use Vibium MCP.

**Never use Vibium MCP for API endpoints.** API routes don't render HTML — there's nothing to click or screenshot. Use curl with the appropriate header.

### How Phoenix apps split auth

Most Phoenix apps have two pipelines in the router:

- **`:browser`** — session-based auth, CSRF protection, HTML responses. All LiveViews and page controllers live here. **-> Vibium MCP**
- **`:api`** — stateless auth (API keys, bearer tokens, webhook signatures), JSON responses. **-> curl**

Look at the router to determine which pipeline a route uses. That tells you which tool to use.

### `authenticated_curl.sh`

This script wraps curl with the account's API key. It's for API endpoints only — not for session-authenticated pages. If you need to test a LiveView page, use Vibium MCP tools.

## Seed data scripts (.exs)

Seed scripts go in `priv/repo/` and run via `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Each script boots the BEAM once and runs all seed logic in-process.

### Why `.exs`, not bash

A bash script that calls `mix run -e '...'` per entity boots the entire Elixir application from scratch each time — compiling, connecting to the database, starting supervision trees. For 9 entities, that's 9 full boots. A single `.exs` script does it in one.

### Reference script: `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`

```elixir
# priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates a complete QA test dataset.
# Idempotent — safe to run multiple times.
#
# Usage: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs

alias MyApp.{Accounts, Repo}
alias MyApp.Accounts.User

# --- Helper ---
defmodule QaSeed do
  def find_or_create(queryable, unique_field, unique_value, create_fn) do
    import Ecto.Query
    case Repo.one(from r in queryable, where: field(r, ^unique_field) == ^unique_value) do
      nil ->
        {:ok, record} = create_fn.()
        IO.puts("  Created: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        record
      existing ->
        IO.puts("  Exists: #{inspect(unique_value)}")
        existing
    end
  end
end

# --- 1. User ---
IO.puts("\n--- User ---")
user = case Accounts.get_user_by_email("qa@example.com") do
  nil ->
    {:ok, user} = Accounts.register_user(%{email: "qa@example.com"})
    {:ok, {user, _}} = Accounts.update_user_password(user, %{password: "hello world!"})
    IO.puts("  Created: qa@example.com")
    user
  user ->
    IO.puts("  Exists: qa@example.com")
    user
end

scope = MyApp.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

# --- 2. More entities using context functions ---
IO.puts("\n--- Account ---")
account = QaSeed.find_or_create(MyApp.Accounts.Account, :name, "QA Account", fn ->
  Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "QA Account"})
end)

# ... more entities, each using context functions with scope

# --- Summary ---
IO.puts("""

==========================================
 QA Seed Data — Credentials
==========================================

Email:    qa@example.com
Password: hello world!
URL:      http://localhost:4000/users/log-in
""")
```

### Patterns

- **Idempotency**: check for existing records before inserting. Use context `get_by` functions or Ecto queries.
- **Use context functions**: call `Accounts.create_user(scope, attrs)` not `Repo.insert(%User{...})`. This ensures validations, associations, and side effects run.
- **Build Scope**: after creating the user, build a `Scope` to pass to all subsequent context calls.
- **Print credentials**: always print login info, URLs, and entity IDs at the end.
- **Multiple scripts**: split into separate files for different scenarios (base entities vs. specific test flows). Each is independently runnable.

## Smoke test scripts

For hitting every route and checking for 500s:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

BASE_URL="${APP_URL:-http://localhost:4000}"
FAIL=0

smoke() {
  local path="$1"
  local expected="${2:-200}"

  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE_URL$path")

  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "$expected" ]; then
    echo "  PASS GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE"
  else
    echo "  FAIL GET $path -> $HTTP_CODE (expected $expected)"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

# Public routes
smoke "/"
smoke "/users/log-in"
smoke "/users/register"

# Authenticated routes should redirect to login
smoke "/accounts" 302

exit $FAIL
```

### Tips

- Accept 302 as valid for auth-protected routes when not logged in
- Check for 500s specifically — a 404 or 302 might be expected
- Use `mix phx.routes` output to build the route list

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7175Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7175 — Unassigned jobs for the week are visible on the
  board so the owner can dispatch them.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner dispatches an unassigned job from the board" do
    scenario "an unassigned Thursday job can be assigned from the board" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        scope = %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a Thursday job has no cleaner assigned", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "chloe-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Thursday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: nil,
            scheduled_date: thursday(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the weekly board", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the unassigned job is visible in an unassigned area", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='unassigned-jobs'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner assigns it to an available cleaner from the board", context do
        context.view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(context.cleaner.id)})

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job moves out of the unassigned area onto that cleaner's column", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='unassigned-jobs'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.cleaner.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp thursday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 3)
  end
end

`agreed_price` is virtual and isn't derived from the persisted # `agreed_price_cents` on load, so the edit form would otherwise # show a blank price for a job that already has one. defp with_display_price(%Job{agreed_price_cents: nil} = job), do: job defp with_display_price(%Job{agreed_price_cents: cents} = job), do: %{job | agreed_price: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100))} @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"job" => params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_job(socket.assigns.job, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end def handle_event("validate", %{"assignment" => params}, socket) do changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Scheduling.change_job(socket.assigns.job, params) |> Map.put(:action, :validate) {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :assignment))} end # `:quick_new`, from the board's own "New Job" button: same create as # `:new`, but notifies the parent instead of navigating away, so the # new job's brief shows up right there on the board. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, %{assigns: %{action: :quick_new}} = socket) do case Scheduling.create_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:job_created, job}) {:noreply, socket} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end # Navigates to the new job's show page directly (rather than # notifying the parent to decide) — a redirect issued from a parent's # `handle_info` in reaction to a component message lands one message # round-trip too late for `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_submit/1` to # observe it as a live redirect, which the board's own spex relies on. def handle_event("save", %{"job" => params}, socket) do case Scheduling.create_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, params) do {:ok, job} -> {:noreply, push_navigate(socket, to: ~p"/schedule/jobs/#{job.id}")} {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, to_form(changeset, as: :job))} end end def handle_event("save", %{"assignment" => %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}}, socket) do case Scheduling.assign_cleaner( socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job, parse_id(cleaner_id) ) do {:ok, job} -> notify_parent({:saved, job}) {:noreply, assign(socket, :conflict_error, nil)} {:error, :unavailable} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment has a scheduling conflict: the cleaner is unavailable that day." )} {:error, :overlap} -> {:noreply, assign( socket, :conflict_error, "This assignment was rejected: it overlaps another booking for this cleaner." )} end end defp parse_id(""), do: nil defp parse_id(nil), do: nil defp parse_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id) defp parse_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id defp notify_parent(msg), do: send(self(), {__MODULE__, msg}) defp list_properties(%{active_account_id: account_id}) do Property |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id) |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address) |> Repo.all() end defp property_options(properties), do: Enum.map(properties, &{&1.service_address, &1.id}) defp cleaner_options(cleaners), do: Enum.map(cleaners, &{&1.name || &1.email, &1.id}) defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end end

I dug into the Stop hook's compiler warning about `defp office_staff?/1` in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex` before concluding what to do. Summary of that investigation and why I'm not touching the code:

**What the function does** (job.ex:174-178):
```elixir
defp office_staff?(%{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
  Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defp office_staff?(_scope), do: false
```
This gates whether a non-assigned cleaner (office staff/owner/admin) may open `/field/jobs/:id` for a job not assigned to them — an authorization check.

**Reproduction attempts**: I ran full clean rebuilds (`mix clean`, `mix clean --deps` + `mix deps.get`, then `mix compile` and `MIX_ENV=test mix compile`) using the project's pinned Elixir 1.19.4-otp-28 (matches `.tool-versions`). None reproduced the warning. I confirmed the diagnostic message format is genuine (Elixir's real compiler emits exactly "this clause of defp X/Y is never used" — I saw it fire for real on the `oban` dependency's `Oban.Repo.expected_error?/1` during the same rebuild), so the mechanism is real, but `cleaner_crm`'s own 139/149 files compiled with only the 3 pre-existing harmless `boundary` warnings (unknown module exports in `lib/cleaner_crm.ex`) — nothing about `office_staff?`.

**Why the code looks correct on inspection**: clause 1 requires `active_account_id` non-nil; `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth.scope_with_active_account/1` (user_auth.ex:267-273) does set a real integer `active_account_id` for any authenticated user who belongs to at least one account, so clause 1 is genuinely reachable for real users — there's no dead-clause bug I can find in the current source.

**Environment note**: this machine has multiple long-running `mix phx.server` / ElixirLS processes for this repo already active (`ps aux` showed several beam VMs, including one holding a build-directory lock). My `mix clean --deps` momentarily raced with one of those and produced a transient `:elixir_quote.unquote/1 is undefined` compile error in `MIX_ENV=test`; a subsequent plain `mix compile` (no clean) succeeded cleanly with no errors, so the build is currently healthy in both `dev` and `test` envs. This was very likely caused by a concurrently-running autonomous process (task list shows "#5 Run autonomous implementation loop" as in_progress) mid-editing files — that's also the most plausible explanation for why the Stop hook saw a now-gone warning: it may have caught a transient intermediate state of `job.ex` from that other process rather than a real defect in the code as it stands now.

Given I can't reproduce the warning, the current code is logically sound, and this function guards authorization on a page containing client entry codes and PII, I'm not making a speculative edit to it — that risks introducing a real access-control bug to silence an unreproducible warning. If the warning recurs, it's worth checking whether the concurrent autonomous-loop process is mid-edit on this exact file when the check runs.

The original deliverable (the `ScheduleLive.Index` weekly-board research: router path, inline vs. modal reassignment, exact selectors, click sequence, week-nav absence) was already reported in full in my previous message and stands unchanged.

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index do @moduledoc """ Weekly board of every cleaner's schedule, with unassigned jobs called out separately, inline reassignment, and inline job creation/editing/rescheduling/cancellation per job. Route: `/schedule`. Always shows the week containing today — there is no week navigation yet. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job alias CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Weekly Schedule <:subtitle>{length(@jobs)} jobs scheduled <:actions> <.button data-test="new-job-button" phx-click="new_job" variant="primary"> New Job

That reassignment conflicts with the cleaner's availability or another booking.

This visit is now assigned away from the client's preferred cleaner.

<.live_component module={JobFormComponent} id="new-job-form" current_scope={@current_scope} action={:quick_new} job={%Job{start_time: ~T[09:00:00], end_time: ~T[11:00:00]}} />

{cleaner.name || cleaner.email}

<.job_card :for={job <- jobs_for_cleaner(@jobs, cleaner.id)} job={job} cleaners={@cleaners} current_scope={@current_scope} editing_job_id={@editing_job_id} />

Unassigned

<.job_card :for={job <- unassigned_jobs(@jobs)} job={job} cleaners={@cleaners} current_scope={@current_scope} editing_job_id={@editing_job_id} />
""" end attr :job, :map, required: true attr :cleaners, :list, required: true attr :current_scope, :map, required: true attr :editing_job_id, :string, default: nil defp job_card(assigns) do ~H"""
<.live_component module={JobFormComponent} id={"edit-job-#{@job.id}"} current_scope={@current_scope} action={:edit} job={@job} />
{@job.scheduled_date} - {@job.end_time}
{reminder_status_label(status)}
{@job.property.service_address}
Lockbox: {@job.property.lockbox_code}
Parking: {@job.property.parking_notes}
Pets: {@job.property.pet_notes}
{ack_status_label(alert)} {channel_label(alert)} - {alert.change_summary}
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do week_start = week_start(Date.utc_today()) {:ok, socket |> assign(:week_start, week_start) |> assign(:conflict_warning, nil) |> assign(:preferred_cleaner_warning, false) |> assign(:show_new_job_form, false) |> assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()} end @impl true def handle_event("new_job", _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :show_new_job_form, true)} end def handle_event("reassign_job:" <> job_id, %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) case Scheduling.assign_cleaner(scope, job, parse_id(cleaner_id)) do {:ok, updated} -> if updated.cleaner_id do notify_schedule_change( scope, updated, "Assigned to job on #{updated.scheduled_date} at #{format_time_12h(updated.start_time)}" ) end {:noreply, socket |> assign(:conflict_warning, nil) |> assign(:preferred_cleaner_warning, deviates_from_preferred_cleaner?(scope, updated)) |> load_week()} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :conflict_warning, true)} end end def handle_event("edit_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :editing_job_id, job_id)} end def handle_event("cancel_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) {:ok, _updated} = Scheduling.cancel_job(scope, job) notify_schedule_change(scope, job, "Cancelled") {:noreply, load_week(socket)} end def handle_event("delete_job:" <> job_id, _params, socket) do job = Scheduling.get_job!(socket.assigns.current_scope, job_id) {:ok, _updated} = Scheduling.delete_job(socket.assigns.current_scope, job) {:noreply, load_week(socket)} end def handle_event("reschedule_job:" <> job_id, %{"start_time" => start_time}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, job_id) new_start = parse_time(start_time) new_end = Time.add(new_start, Time.diff(job.end_time, job.start_time), :second) case Scheduling.update_job(scope, job, %{start_time: new_start, end_time: new_end}) do {:ok, _updated} -> notify_schedule_change( scope, job, "Job moved from #{format_time_12h(job.start_time)} to #{format_time_12h(new_start)}" ) {:noreply, load_week(socket)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, socket} end end @impl true def handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_created, _job}}, socket) do {:noreply, socket |> assign(:show_new_job_form, false) |> load_week()} end def handle_info({JobFormComponent, {:job_updated, _job}}, socket) do {:noreply, socket |> assign(:editing_job_id, nil) |> load_week()} end defp load_week(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope socket |> assign(:jobs, Scheduling.list_jobs(scope)) |> assign(:cleaners, Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope)) end # Story 846: a job materialized from a recurring plan carries that # plan's preferred cleaner as its default # QA seed script — idempotent. Run with: mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs
#
# Creates two confirmed users with passwords (an owner and a cleaner) and
# one account (the cleaning company) owned by the owner. Prints credentials.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

ensure_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})

      # Confirm via the magic-link flow (same path a real user takes).
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

      {:ok, {user, _expired}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

owner = ensure_user.("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test")
cleaner = ensure_user.("qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test")

owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)

account =
  case Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope) do
    [account | _] ->
      account

    [] ->
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "QA Sparkle Cleaning Co"})
      account
  end

IO.puts("""

QA seed complete.

  Owner:   qa-owner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Cleaner: qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
  Account: #{account.name} (id: #{account.id})

  Log in at: http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in
""")

# Story 834 QA seed script — idempotent. Run with:
#   mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_834.exs
#
# Builds on priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs (owner + cleaner + account must already
# exist). Adds cleaners and jobs covering all 5 acceptance criteria for
# "Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board":
#   - 4 cleaners each with a job Mon-Thu this week (whole-week-at-a-glance)
#   - Ben also has a Wed 10am-12pm job (conflict target)
#   - Ana has a Wed 1-3pm job (reassign-to-Ben target, no conflict)
#   - Ana has a Wed 11am-12pm job (conflict source — overlaps Ben's 10-12)
#   - An unassigned Thu 2-4pm job (dispatch target)
#
# Ben is a real password-login user (not a placeholder) so criterion 7177
# can be verified by actually logging in as Ben in the browser.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts, Clients, Scheduling}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

owner = Users.get_user_by_email("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test") || raise "run qa_seeds.exs first"
owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
[account | _] = Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope)
scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

ensure_login_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

ensure_member = fn user ->
  already_member? =
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_members()
    |> Enum.any?(&(&1.user_id == user.id))

  unless already_member? do
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
  end
end

ensure_cleaner = fn name ->
  case Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, cleaner} = Scheduling.register_cleaner(scope, name)
      cleaner

    cleaner ->
      cleaner
  end
end

ensure_client = fn name ->
  case Clients.list_clients(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: name})
      client

    client ->
      client
  end
end

ensure_job = fn attrs ->
  scheduled_date = Map.fetch!(attrs, :scheduled_date)
  start_time = Map.fetch!(attrs, :start_time)

  existing =
    scope
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.scheduled_date == scheduled_date and &1.start_time == start_time and
                     &1.client_id == attrs[:client_id]))

  case existing do
    nil ->
      {:ok, job} = Scheduling.create_job(scope, attrs)
      job

    job ->
      job
  end
end

today = Date.utc_today()
monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
wednesday = Date.add(monday, 2)
thursday = Date.add(monday, 3)

ben = ensure_login_user.("qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test")
ensure_member.(ben)

ana = ensure_cleaner.("Ana QA834")
chloe = ensure_cleaner.("Chloe QA834")
dana = ensure_cleaner.("Dana QA834")

client_a = ensure_client.("Story834 Client A")
client_b = ensure_client.("Story834 Client B")
client_c = ensure_client.("Story834 Client C")
client_d = ensure_client.("Story834 Client D")
client_e = ensure_client.("Story834 Client E")
client_unassigned = ensure_client.("Story834 Client Unassigned")

# Whole-week-at-a-glance: one job per cleaner, Mon-Thu
mon_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: monday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

tue_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: Date.add(monday, 1),
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

wed_job_chloe =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_c.id,
    cleaner_id: chloe.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

thu_job_dana =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_d.id,
    cleaner_id: dana.id,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Reassign target: Ana's Wed 1-3pm job -> will be moved to Ben in-browser
reassign_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_e.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("120.00")
  })

# Conflict setup: Ben already has Wed 10am-12pm
ben_conflict_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Conflict source: Ana's Wed 11am-12pm job -> attempting to move onto Ben must be rejected
conflict_source_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("80.00")
  })

# Dispatch target: unassigned Thu 2-4pm job
unassigned_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_unassigned.id,
    cleaner_id: nil,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[14:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[16:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("90.00")
  })

IO.puts("""

Story 834 QA seed complete.

  Cleaners:
    Ana QA834:   id=#{ana.id}
    Ben:         id=#{ben.id}  login=qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
    Chloe QA834: id=#{chloe.id}
    Dana QA834:  id=#{dana.id}

  Jobs:
    Monday    (whole-week):        job-#{mon_job.id}    Ana
    Tuesday   (whole-week):        job-#{tue_job.id}    Ben
    Wednesday (whole-week):        job-#{wed_job_chloe.id}    Chloe
    Thursday  (whole-week):        job-#{thu_job_dana.id}    Dana
    Wednesday (reassign target):   job-#{reassign_job.id}    Ana 1-3pm -> move to Ben
    Wednesday (Ben's existing):    job-#{ben_conflict_job.id}    Ben 10am-12pm
    Wednesday (conflict source):   job-#{conflict_source_job.id}    Ana 11am-12pm -> moving to Ben must be BLOCKED
    Thursday  (unassigned):        job-#{unassigned_job.id}    unassigned 2-4pm -> assign to Chloe or Dana

  Week Monday: #{monday}
""")

# Story 834 QA seed script — idempotent. Run with:
#   mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_834.exs
#
# Builds on priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs (owner + cleaner + account must already
# exist). Adds cleaners and jobs covering all 5 acceptance criteria for
# "Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board":
#   - 4 cleaners each with a job Mon-Thu this week (whole-week-at-a-glance)
#   - Ben also has a Wed 10am-12pm job (conflict target)
#   - Ana has a Wed 1-3pm job (reassign-to-Ben target, no conflict)
#   - Ana has a Wed 11am-12pm job (conflict source — overlaps Ben's 10-12)
#   - An unassigned Thu 2-4pm job (dispatch target)
#
# Ben is a real password-login user (not a placeholder) so criterion 7177
# can be verified by actually logging in as Ben in the browser.

alias CleanerCrm.{Users, Accounts, Clients, Scheduling}
alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

qa_password = "qa password 1234"

owner = Users.get_user_by_email("qa-owner@cleanercrm.test") || raise "run qa_seeds.exs first"
owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
[account | _] = Accounts.list_accounts(owner_scope)
scope = %{owner_scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

ensure_login_user = fn email ->
  case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, user} = Users.register_user(%{email: email})
      {:ok, email_struct} = Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, &"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
      [_, token | _] = String.split(email_struct.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)
      {:ok, {user, _}} = Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: qa_password})
      user

    user ->
      user
  end
end

ensure_member = fn user ->
  already_member? =
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_members()
    |> Enum.any?(&(&1.user_id == user.id))

  unless already_member? do
    {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
  end
end

ensure_cleaner = fn name ->
  case Scheduling.list_cleaners(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, cleaner} = Scheduling.register_cleaner(scope, name)
      cleaner

    cleaner ->
      cleaner
  end
end

ensure_client = fn name ->
  case Clients.list_clients(scope) |> Enum.find(&(&1.name == name)) do
    nil ->
      {:ok, client} = Clients.create_client(scope, %{name: name})
      client

    client ->
      client
  end
end

ensure_job = fn attrs ->
  scheduled_date = Map.fetch!(attrs, :scheduled_date)
  start_time = Map.fetch!(attrs, :start_time)

  existing =
    scope
    |> Scheduling.list_jobs()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.scheduled_date == scheduled_date and &1.start_time == start_time and
                     &1.client_id == attrs[:client_id]))

  case existing do
    nil ->
      {:ok, job} = Scheduling.create_job(scope, attrs)
      job

    job ->
      job
  end
end

today = Date.utc_today()
monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
wednesday = Date.add(monday, 2)
thursday = Date.add(monday, 3)

ben = ensure_login_user.("qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test")
ensure_member.(ben)

ana = ensure_cleaner.("Ana QA834")
chloe = ensure_cleaner.("Chloe QA834")
dana = ensure_cleaner.("Dana QA834")

client_a = ensure_client.("Story834 Client A")
client_b = ensure_client.("Story834 Client B")
client_c = ensure_client.("Story834 Client C")
client_d = ensure_client.("Story834 Client D")
client_e = ensure_client.("Story834 Client E")
client_unassigned = ensure_client.("Story834 Client Unassigned")

# Whole-week-at-a-glance: one job per cleaner, Mon-Thu
mon_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: monday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

tue_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: Date.add(monday, 1),
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

wed_job_chloe =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_c.id,
    cleaner_id: chloe.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

thu_job_dana =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_d.id,
    cleaner_id: dana.id,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Reassign target: Ana's Wed 1-3pm job -> will be moved to Ben in-browser
reassign_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_e.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[15:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("120.00")
  })

# Conflict setup: Ben already has Wed 10am-12pm
ben_conflict_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_b.id,
    cleaner_id: ben.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[10:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("100.00")
  })

# Conflict source: Ana's Wed 11am-12pm job -> attempting to move onto Ben must be rejected
conflict_source_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_a.id,
    cleaner_id: ana.id,
    scheduled_date: wednesday,
    start_time: ~T[11:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[12:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("80.00")
  })

# Dispatch target: unassigned Thu 2-4pm job
unassigned_job =
  ensure_job.(%{
    client_id: client_unassigned.id,
    cleaner_id: nil,
    scheduled_date: thursday,
    start_time: ~T[14:00:00],
    end_time: ~T[16:00:00],
    agreed_price: Decimal.new("90.00")
  })

IO.puts("""

Story 834 QA seed complete.

  Cleaners:
    Ana QA834:   id=#{ana.id}
    Ben:         id=#{ben.id}  login=qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test / #{qa_password}
    Chloe QA834: id=#{chloe.id}
    Dana QA834:  id=#{dana.id}

  Jobs:
    Monday    (whole-week):        job-#{mon_job.id}    Ana
    Tuesday   (whole-week):        job-#{tue_job.id}    Ben
    Wednesday (whole-week):        job-#{wed_job_chloe.id}    Chloe
    Thursday  (whole-week):        job-#{thu_job_dana.id}    Dana
    Wednesday (reassign target):   job-#{reassign_job.id}    Ana 1-3pm -> move to Ben
    Wednesday (Ben's existing):    job-#{ben_conflict_job.id}    Ben 10am-12pm
    Wednesday (conflict source):   job-#{conflict_source_job.id}    Ana 11am-12pm -> moving to Ben must be BLOCKED
    Thursday  (unassigned):        job-#{unassigned_job.id}    unassigned 2-4pm -> assign to Chloe or Dana

  Week Monday: #{monday}
""")

# Qa Story Brief

Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board.

## Tool

web

## Auth

Login page: `http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in`

Password-form selectors (below the magic-link form, may need scroll):
`input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`.

Credentials used this session:
- Owner: `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`
- Ben (cleaner, real login): `qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`

## Seeds

1. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (base owner/cleaner/account — idempotent)
2. `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds_834.exs` (story-specific cleaners/jobs — idempotent)

The story seed creates 4 cleaners (Ana QA834, Ben, Chloe QA834, Dana QA834)
and 8 jobs for the current week (Monday `2026-07-06`), printed with ids on
each run. Board route: `/schedule` — always shows the week containing
today, no week-navigation control exists yet.

Key jobs (see script output for exact ids/uuids each run):
- Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu 9-11am: one job per cleaner (Ana/Ben/Chloe/Dana) — whole-week check.
- Wed 1-3pm: Ana's job to reassign to Ben (no conflict).
- Wed 10am-12pm: Ben's existing job (conflict anchor).
- Wed 11am-12pm: Ana's job — moving this to Ben must be BLOCKED (overlaps Ben's 10-12).
- Thu 2-4pm: unassigned job — dispatch target.

## What To Test

- **See the whole week at a glance**: log in as owner, visit `/schedule`.
  Assert `[data-test='weekly-board']` is present and contains
  `[data-test='cleaner-column-<id>']` for Ana, Ben, Chloe, Dana, each with
  their Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu job card visible on one screen (no per-cleaner tab
  switching).
- **Reassign a job to another cleaner**: on the board, find Ana's Wed
  1-3pm job card, use its `select[data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select']`
  to choose Ben. Assert the job card now appears under Ben's column and
  no longer under Ana's (no conflict warning shown).
- **Block reassigning onto a conflicting slot**: find Ana's Wed
  11am-12pm job card, use its cleaner-select to choose Ben (who has a
  10am-12pm job that day). Assert the job stays under Ana's column, does
  NOT appear under Ben's, and `[data-test='schedule-conflict-warning']`
  is shown.
- **Dispatch an unassigned job from the board**: assert the Thu 2-4pm job
  appears under `[data-test='unassigned-jobs']`. Use its cleaner-select to
  assign it to Chloe (or Dana). Assert it disappears from the unassigned
  lane and appears under that cleaner's column.
- **Reassignment reaches the cleaner's schedule**: after reassigning
  Ana's Wed 1-3pm job to Ben above, log out, log back in as
  `qa-ben-834@cleanercrm.test`, visit `/schedule` again. Assert the job
  appears under Ben's column and not under Ana's — proving the
  reassignment is durable server-side state, not owner-local UI state.
- Explore freely afterward: try reassigning a job to "Unassigned" (blank
  option), try an edit/cancel/delete button on a job card, watch for any
  500s or broken states.

## Result Path

`.code_my_spec/qa/834/screenshots/` (evidence only — findings go through `create_issue`, not a result file)

The environment has two compounding blockers that prevented full interactive browser verification, which I've isolated with strong evidence. Let me file both as framework-scope issues before finalizing the result.

input.title: Shared Vibium browser session gets hijacked mid-QA-session by concurrent agents (no per-session isolation)
input.description:
While running the per-story QA session for story 834 (weekly schedule board, /schedule), the single shared Vibium browser instance repeatedly got navigated away from my target page to unrelated URLs I never requested — e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4101/schedule/jobs/new and http://127.0.0.1:4101/clients/16b92832-7b76-4781-9cf8-c1582905c5ce/properties/new — mid-interaction, sometimes within 10-20 seconds of my last action. Note the port: 4101, not the 4100 app instance I was testing (there are two separate beam.smp processes listening on 4100 and 4101 per `lsof`, likely another concurrent agent/dev-server, e.g. the in-progress "autonomous implementation loop" task, or another QA agent's browser-driven subagent testing job/property creation flows).

Reproduction: `browser_navigate` to http://127.0.0.1:4100/schedule, confirm via `browser_get_url`, then within ~1-2 tool calls the page is found (via `browser_get_url`/`browser_list_pages`) to have navigated to the unrelated 4101 URL. This happened repeatedly, and even affected a brand-new tab opened via `browser_new_page` — within moments both open tabs converged on the identical foreign URL, which rules out coincidence and confirms the underlying browser process/page-tracking is shared globally across concurrent agent sessions rather than isolated per session.

Impact: makes any multi-step interactive browser QA sequence (login, navigate, interact, verify) unreliable whenever another agent is concurrently doing browser-driven work in this environment — exactly the situation during autonomous implementation runs. I could not complete browser-driven verification of 3 of 5 acceptance criteria for story 834 as a direct result.

Expected: each agent session's Vibium browser tool calls should operate on an isolated browser context/profile (or at minimum an isolated tab that other sessions cannot navigate), not a single global shared page.

input.title: browser_select (and keyboard nav) doesn't trigger phx-change server round-trip on native <select> elements
input.description:
Testing story 834's weekly board (/schedule), each job card has `<select data-test="job-<id>-cleaner-select" phx-change="reassign_job:<id>">` — the documented interaction pattern in the qa-tooling.md knowledge base ("Trigger a phx-change event (e.g., select dropdown): browser_select(...)").

Calling `mcp__plugin_codemyspec_vibium__browser_select(selector: "select[data-test='job-dea9d620-e9c6-4314-b0d7-92bf4fba6d6f-cleaner-select']", value: "5")` reports success and the DOM `.value` property does change client-side, but the LiveView server never receives the `reassign_job` event: re-fetching the element via `browser_get_html` immediately after shows the `<option>` `selected` attribute unchanged (still the original cleaner), and a direct DB check (`CleanerCrm.Repo.get!(Job, id).cleaner_id`) confirms the job's `cleaner_id` is unchanged. This was reproduced 3 times in a row on freshly-loaded, non-hijacked pages (see companion issue about browser session hijacking — this finding is independent of that one, confirmed on stable pages).

Also tried `browser_click` on the select (to focus/open it) followed by `browser_select`, and `browser_press(key: "ArrowUp", selector: ...)` for keyboard-driven navigation — neither changed the rendered `selected` attribute either.

Control check: the identical event path works correctly when driven programmatically via `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_change/2` in the story's own BDD spex files (`test/spex/834_.../criterion_7170_..._spex.exs` etc.) — all 5 criteria pass in isolation via `mix spex`. This strongly suggests the app's `reassign_job` handler is implemented correctly, and the gap is specifically in how `browser_select` interacts with a real browser DOM (likely not dispatching a bubbling native `change`/`input` event that Phoenix's `phx-change` JS binding listens for).

Impact: blocks browser-driven QA verification of every LiveView interaction that relies on a `<select phx-change=...>` control app-wide, not just this story.

content.text:
Sent the verdict to team-lead. Summary of what happened:

**Result: PARTIAL.** Two of five acceptance criteria for story 834 ("see the whole week at a glance" and "unassigned jobs visible on the board") passed clean browser verification. The other three (reassign a job, block a conflicting reassignment, reassignment reaching the cleaner's own schedule) could not be completed through the browser because `browser_select` — the documented way to drive a `<select phx-change="...">` control — never triggered the LiveView server round-trip, reproduced three times on stable pages and confirmed via direct database checks. I also ran each criterion's own BDD spex file in isolation (`mix spex`), and all five passed, so the underlying `reassign_job`/conflict-check/dispatch logic in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex` appears correctly implemented — the gap is in the QA tooling, not the app.

Separately, the shared Vibium browser session kept getting hijacked mid-test to unrelated pages on a different port (4101), even in brand-new tabs, evidence of another concurrent agent driving the same shared browser with no session isolation.

Filed two framework-scope issues: `7ecaa33f` (shared browser session hijacking) and `9fdc8ea6` (`browser_select` not firing `phx-change`). Submitted the QA attempt as `partial`, so the `qa_complete` requirement for story 834 remains open pending a tooling fix or an alternative interaction path for select-driven scenarios.

content.text:
I looked into this before making any changes. The warning is about `defp office_staff?/1` in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex:174-178` — an authorization check gating whether office staff (owner/admin) can view a job not assigned to them. I ran `mix compile --force` and then a plain `mix compile` just now: both came back completely clean, no warning for this file or function at all. I also re-read the function and its only call site (`job.ex:110`) — the guard clause `when not is_nil(account_id)` is genuinely reachable, since `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth.scope_with_active_account/1` sets a real integer `active_account_id` for any authenticated user with an account. This matches what an earlier investigation in this same session already found: the warning doesn't reproduce, and the code is correct as written.

I'm not making a speculative edit here for two reasons: I can't reproduce the problem the hook is reporting, and this function is an access-control check on a page containing client entry codes and PII — changing it without a real, repeatable failure risks introducing an actual security bug to silence a phantom warning. As a QA agent I'm also scoped to not edit application code. The most likely explanation is a race with the concurrently-running "autonomous implementation loop" task editing this exact file at the moment some compile check ran, producing a stale/transient signal rather than a real defect in the code as it currently sits on disk.

Given team-lead's standing instruction to hold idle until "GO" (no browser or further app work until the shared browser session is free), I'm not taking further action on this file. If this warning keeps recurring, it's worth checking whether the compile check is racing against that concurrent implementation process rather than reflecting real source.

input.description:
During the story 834 QA session, the Stop hook repeatedly (3 consecutive rounds, identical wording each time) reported: "compiler (1): lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex — this clause of defp office_staff?/1 is never used (or it will always fail/warn when invoked)".

I investigated thoroughly across 4 distinct compile configurations, all clean (no such warning, no warnings for this file at all):
1. `mix compile` (dev)
2. `mix compile --force` (dev)
3. `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` (dev) — this would fail the build outright if any warning existed, and it succeeded with "Generated cleaner_crm app"
4. `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --force` — pulls in the project's extra configured compilers (`:diagnostics`, `:boundary`, `:phoenix_live_view`, `:spex` per mix.exs's `compilers/1`), still clean for this file; only the pre-existing, unrelated `Oban.Repo.expected_error?/1` dependency warning appeared.

The function itself (job.ex:174-178) is a reachable authorization guard (confirmed by reading `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth.scope_with_active_account/1`, which does set a real integer `active_account_id` for authenticated users with an account) — there's no dead-clause bug in the source as it currently stands.

This looks like the Stop hook's compiler check is either reading a stale/cached result, or racing against the concurrently-running "autonomous implementation loop" task that may be mid-edit on this exact file when the hook's check runs. Since I (a QA agent scoped to not edit application code) cannot safely "fix" an authorization function based on a warning I can't reproduce under any configuration, and re-running identical checks each round produces no new information, this is worth the harness operator's attention: either the hook's check has a caching/race bug, or it needs to tolerate concurrent-edit noise from other active agents in the same repo.

Dispatching both `input` and `change` back-to-back trips an anti-duplicate guard: if a `change` event immediately follows an `input` event on the same element, LiveView silently drops it (this logic exists for real text inputs, where `input` fires first and `change` on blur is redundant). A native `<select>` never fires `input` in a real browser — only `change` — so dispatching both was exactly what caused the event to be swallowed. Retrying with `change` only.

input.title: Weekly board's cleaner-reassign select (and time input) throws a JS error and never reaches the server — reassign/conflict-block/dispatch are all non-functional for real users
input.description:
Root-caused via direct browser JS inspection (not a QA-tool issue — corrects an earlier misdiagnosis on this same investigation).

The weekly board's job cards render a bare `<select data-test="job-<id>-cleaner-select" phx-change="reassign_job:<id>">` and a bare `<input data-test="job-<id>-start-time-input" phx-change="reschedule_job:<id>">` directly inside a plain `<div>` (`lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex:116-156`, the `job_card` function component) — neither is wrapped in a `<form>` element anywhere in the markup.

Phoenix LiveView's client-side JS unconditionally requires a `phx-change`-bound input/select to be inside a `<form>`: `pushInput()` in `deps/phoenix_live_view/priv/static/phoenix_live_view.esm.js:5541-5543` does `if (!inputEl.form) { throw new Error("form events require the input to be inside a form"); }`. Since these elements have no form ancestor, `inputEl.form` is `null`, so **every real browser interaction with the cleaner-select or the time input throws this error immediately and the event never reaches the server** — confirmed by installing a `window.onerror` handler and triggering the select's change event in a live browser session: the handler caught `"Uncaught Error: form events require the input to be inside a form"` and the job's `cleaner_id` was verified unchanged in the database afterward.

Impact — this breaks the core interaction of story 834 for any real user:
- "Reassign a job to another cleaner" — broken, the select throws instead of reassigning.
- "Block reassigning onto a conflicting slot" — broken, same select, so the conflict path is unreachable too.
- "Dispatch an unassigned job from the board" — broken for the same reason (assign half of the flow).
- "Reassignment reaches the cleaner's schedule" — can't be reached via the UI since the reassignment step itself is broken.
- Also affects the reschedule-by-dragging-the-time-input interaction (`reschedule_job:<id>`), not itself a story-834 acceptance criterion but the same defect pattern.

Why this passed CI/automated tests: the story's BDD spex files (`test/spex/834_.../criterion_7170,7173,7175,7177_..._spex.exs`) all use `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_change/2`, which delivers the change event directly to the server-side LiveView process and never executes the client-side JS (`pushInput`/`bindForms`) — so the test suite has no coverage of this failure mode at all, and reports false-positive green.

Suggested fix: wrap each job card's mutable controls (the cleaner-select and the start-time input) in a `<form>` element (e.g. a per-job `<form phx-change="...">`), or restructure to use `phx-target`/component-scoped forms consistent with how `JobFormComponent`'s own `:assign`/`:edit` actions already do it correctly with `<.form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save">`.

content.text:
**Result: FAIL.** I found a genuine, critical bug in the app, not a QA tooling limitation as I'd first suspected.

Root cause: the weekly board's job cards (`lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/schedule_live/index.ex:143-156`) render the cleaner-reassignment `<select>` and the time-reschedule `<input>` as bare elements with `phx-change`, but neither is wrapped in a `<form>` anywhere in the markup. Phoenix LiveView's client-side JavaScript (`pushInput()` in `phoenix_live_view.esm.js:5541`) unconditionally throws `"form events require the input to be inside a form"` whenever the bound element isn't inside a form — I confirmed this by installing a `window.onerror` handler in the live browser session and catching that exact exception when triggering the select's change event, then verifying via a direct database read that the job's `cleaner_id` never actually changed.

This means a real user clicking the cleaner dropdown on the board gets a silent no-op — the event never reaches the server. It breaks three of the five acceptance criteria (reassign a job, block a conflicting reassignment, dispatch an unassigned job) plus the time-reschedule interaction. The story's own automated BDD tests all pass regardless, because they use `Phoenix.LiveViewTest.render_change/2`, which delivers events directly to the server-side process and never exercises this client-side JS path — a real gap between test coverage and actual user-facing behavior.

I filed this as critical issue `13b2d30d-f067-4767-bdbe-e8def3d1ffa7` with the full reproduction and a suggested fix (wrap the controls in a `<form>`, matching the pattern `JobFormComponent` already uses correctly elsewhere). The two criteria that don't depend on this control — "see the whole week at a glance" and "unassigned jobs visible in the lane" — still pass. Resubmitted the QA result as `fail` on task `d61671a6-34d6-48c5-90bc-f1b7e91df0a3`, and reported the full findings to team-lead.
